findings.kind: rank floor / incomplete configuration-time authority check
findings.title: The wake arm checks the directing member's membership STATUS but not their ROLE RANK, so a demoted member's standing instruction still configures plans that can never post a single occurrence
findings.evidence: 0338 §F's lapse branch is 'if not exists (select 1 from clara.firm_memberships m where m.firm_id = p_firm and m.user_id = v_directing and m.status = 'active')' (packages/db/migrations/0338_prepayment_close_standing_instruction.sql:845-847) — status only. clara._admit_accounting_work_core, which every occurrence goes through, additionally requires clara.role_rank(v_role) >= clara.role_rank('bookkeeper') and raises CLR04 'recording a journal entry requires a bookkeeper or above'. DRIVEN on clara_l05: a scene recorded its instruction as the owner, the owner was then demoted to 'viewer' (still status='active', a second owner promoted first past _tf_guard_last_owner), and the clocked lane CONFIGURED schedule bc572eab-1e97-451c-97b5-5c5f6733d6ee / plan 47a78680-a96c-4de1-aacd-d56d57cf0b2a with authority_kind='standing_instruction' and authorised_by = the viewer; clara._plan_admit_occurrence then answered {admitted:false, code:'CLR04', reason:'insufficient_role'} for BOTH 2025-02-28 and 2025-03-31. Memberships restored and re-read. This is exactly the state §F's own comment says the lapse branch exists to prevent: 'A plan is admitted every month AS this person ... configuring something that can never run is worse than refusing'. p1050.wake.lapsed only drives status='removed'.
findings.required_fix: Extend §F's lapse test to the rank clara._admit_accounting_work_core requires (active membership AND role_rank >= bookkeeper), keep the wake_authority_lapsed token, and add a cell that demotes rather than removes.

findings.kind: idempotency under replay / the authority wall sits in front of the reservation
findings.title: A replay of a clocked wake that ALREADY SUCCEEDED stops returning its own receipt once the instruction is withdrawn, and is told the schedule was never configured
findings.evidence: 0338 §F answers the standing-instruction wall before clara._reserve_op ('AND IT IS STILL ANSWERED FIRST, before the purpose wall and before the reservation', packages/db/migrations/0338_prepayment_close_standing_instruction.sql:808-810). DRIVEN on clara_l05: a firm recorded its instruction; wake12 on task c72c1ffd configured schedule 028cb6ac-3d9c-4fe8-9d9c-62ca754a26b4; an immediate replay of the same task returned the SAME schedule from the receipt; the firm then withdrew the instruction through clara.withdraw_firm_standing_instruction; the same task replayed answered CLR03 wake_authority_absent, 'an unattended close_prep wake names no directing human, so it cannot authorise an amortisation plan' — while clara.op_receipts still holds create_prepayment_schedule / op_key 882ea076... with a non-null result and the client still holds 1 schedule. The body's own law for the duplicate check ('A REPLAY OF THE SAME DECISION MUST WIN OVER "THAT PREPAYMENT ALREADY HAS A SCHEDULE" ... a lost response turned into a second refusal') applies verbatim to this wall and is not honoured. The same hole exists for wake_authority_lapsed. It is NEW with this ticket: before 0338 the wake lane always refused, so there was never a successful receipt to replay.
findings.required_fix: Take the reservation before the standing-instruction wall (or consult the receipt first and short-circuit on a completed one), so a replayed task gets its own answer back; then drive the sequence success -> withdraw -> replay in a cell.

findings.title: The reservation census is read with limit 1 and no order by, so which register a refusal names is arbitrary when a code carries two claims
findings.evidence: clara._fa_role_claim_conflict selects 'from clara._acct_role_reserved(p_client, p_code) rr where (rr.domain is distinct from 'fa' or rr.role is distinct from p_want_role) limit 1' with no ORDER BY, and 0337 §C/§D/§E branch on the single v_res_domain it returns. One code enrolled under BOTH roster purposes yields two domain='prepayment' rows (nothing refuses the second purpose: the posting wall skips the prepayment domain by 0337 §B), and a legacy code held by two domains would name an arbitrary register and an arbitrary release door. Harmless today because both roster rows carry the same domain; it becomes a wrong-remedy bug the moment a code legitimately carries two domains.
findings.required_fix: Add a deterministic ORDER BY (domain, role) to the census read inside clara._fa_role_claim_conflict when that body is next recut; not this ticket's to change, so file it.

findings.kind: redo marker is a bare four-digit substring
findings.title: All four migrations admit the redo branch on position('03NN' in prosrc) > 0, which any later body that merely mentions the number satisfies
findings.evidence: 0335:111, 0336:120, 0337:205 and 0338:143 all read 'elsif position('03NN' in v_src) > 0 then ... REDO'. Nothing anchors it to the attribution form the files actually write ('#1114 [0335]', '#1050 (0338 §E)'). Migration headers in this family routinely name their predecessors — 0338's own header says 'current cut 0317 §A, unmoved by 0335, 0336 and 0337' — so the next recut of any of these bodies will carry a string that satisfies an earlier file's redo test. The exposure is bounded (CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO only ever targets the highest applied version, and a from-scratch chain never reaches the branch), which is why this is a note and not a defect: no live path takes the false positive today.
findings.required_fix: When this idiom is next copied, match the file's own attribution marker (e.g. position('[0335]' in v_src) or '#1114 [0335]') rather than the bare number.
